answer: Instagram SEO means making your account findable in Instagram's own search and in Google. The work is concrete: rewrite the 30-character name field, put buyer language in captions and alt text, keep on-screen text readable, and drop hashtag bloat. It sits inside our organic social retainer from ₹30,000 a month.
takeaways: The **name field** — the 30-character display line, not the handle and not the bio — is the single most searchable piece of text on your profile. Most Indian brands waste it on their own name twice.
Instagram reads captions, alt text and on-screen words. Your reel about "bridal makeup in Bandra" needs those words written somewhere a machine can read them.
Hashtags are a filing system now, not a reach lever. Instagram has said so out loud. Ten relevant ones beat thirty desperate ones, and a restricted tag can quietly cap the post.
Public professional-account posts can be indexed by Google, which means your reels compete on a second search engine you don't control and can't measure in your own Search Console.

sections.h2: The name field is the ranking real estate. The bio isn't.
body: Here's the thing almost every Indian brand gets backwards. The bio — the 150 characters under your name, the one everybody agonises over — barely does anything in Instagram search. It converts a visitor who already arrived. It doesn't bring one.

The **name field** does. That's the bold 30-character line above your bio, separate from your @handle, and Instagram's search matches against it directly. Same for the handle itself. If someone types "pilates indiranagar" into Instagram, the accounts with those words in the name field are the ones that surface — not the ones with a beautifully written bio containing the same words.

So we rewrite it. Brand name, then the category and the place, inside 30 characters. It's unglamorous and it takes ten minutes, and it's routinely the difference between an account discovered by search and an account discovered by nobody.

callout.title: Don't stuff the handle
callout.body: Changing your @handle breaks every link anyone has ever shared to your profile, and Instagram doesn't redirect the old one. Put the keywords in the name field, which you can edit freely, and leave the handle alone unless it's genuinely unrecognisable.

sections.h2: Captions, alt text and the words on the screen
body: Instagram's search reads text. It cannot watch your reel. So every signal about what a post is *about* has to exist as words somewhere, and there are three places to put them.

**Captions** carry the most weight. The first line does double duty — it's what search matches and what stops the scroll. We write it with the phrase a buyer would actually type, not the phrase your brand deck prefers. "Bridal makeup Bandra, booking for December" beats "✨ that pre-wedding glow ✨" for everything except vanity.

**Alt text** is a 100-character field you can write yourself on any image post, under advanced settings. Instagram auto-generates one if you don't, and the auto version describes pixels — "may be an image of one person and text". Writing it yourself takes fifteen seconds and gives the machine an accurate sentence instead of a guess.

**On-screen text** in reels gets read too, which is why the first frame matters more than the hook line most agencies obsess over. Put the topic on screen in the first second, in a font a machine can parse, and you've told both the viewer and the index what this is.

sections.h2: Hashtags in 2026: fewer, and none of the desperate ones
body: Hashtags used to be a distribution channel. They aren't anymore. Instagram removed the ability to follow a hashtag at the end of 2024, and Adam Mosseri has said publicly that piling on hashtags doesn't increase reach. What they still do is categorise the post and make it retrievable in tag search — useful, but a filing label rather than an amplifier.

Which means the calculus changes. You're not fishing for reach, you're describing the post accurately to a database. Somewhere between five and ten specific tags does that job. Thirty does not do it three times better.
bullets: **Specific over broad.** `#pilatesindiranagar` retrieves. `#fitness` puts you behind forty million posts and a wall of bots.
**Mix intent levels.** A category tag, a location tag, a product tag, a couple of community tags. That's a complete description of the post.

**Avoid engagement-bait tags.** `#followforfollow`, `#like4like` and their cousins attract bot engagement and sit near tags Instagram has restricted for policy violations. A restricted tag can limit where the post is shown, and Instagram won't tell you it happened.
**Check before you reuse a set.** Tags get restricted quietly. Tap it, and if the recent posts tab is missing or empty, drop it.

callout.title: The comment-versus-caption argument
callout.body: Putting hashtags in the first comment instead of the caption makes no measurable difference to reach. It's purely a tidiness preference. Anyone selling it as a growth tactic is selling you a formatting choice.

sections.h2: Your public posts are now Google's problem too
body: Instagram made public content from professional accounts eligible for indexing by Google, with a setting in your account privacy controls that lets you opt out. That's a genuine shift, and most brands haven't noticed it.

The upside: a well-captioned reel can turn up in a Google search, months after it stopped mattering inside Instagram. Instagram URLs are strong pages on a very strong domain, and for a young brand they sometimes rank for queries your own website can't touch yet.

The catch: you can't measure it. Those URLs live on instagram.com, so they never appear in your Search Console. We track them by running the queries manually and rank-tracking the specific post URLs, which is laborious and honest — as opposed to a dashboard number that looks precise and is invented.

This is also the argument for treating Instagram captions like page copy. If a reel might be indexed, the caption is body text, and "link in bio 🔥" is a blank page. See [how to do SEO on Instagram](/answers/how-to-do-seo-on-instagram) for the version you can run yourself.

sections.h2: The baseline we freeze, and what the guarantee actually says
body: Every engagement we run is settled against a number frozen on day one, in writing, before anyone touches an account. For social work that number is **search-sourced profile visits over the trailing 90 days** — the visits your professional dashboard attributes to search and discovery rather than to your existing followers.

We freeze non-follower reach alongside it as the leading indicator, because it moves first, usually inside four to six weeks. If both are flat at week eight, the pillar choice is wrong and we'd rather rewrite the plan than keep shipping to a schedule.

The guarantee is the same everywhere on this site and it's worth stating precisely: we never promise a specific ranking position or a specific follower count. We commit to beating your own frozen 90-day baseline within 90 days, and if we miss it we keep working free until we beat it. That's also why we only take three new clients a month — you can't carry that risk at volume.
If your buyers are on LinkedIn rather than Instagram, the same logic applies to a different surface entirely — see [LinkedIn SEO services](/services/linkedin-seo-services).

callout.title: Where Instagram SEO won't help
callout.body: If nobody searches for your category on Instagram, optimising for Instagram search optimises for zero. High-consideration B2B, industrial supply and most professional services fall here. We'll tell you during the first call rather than after the third invoice.

faqs.q: Does Instagram SEO actually work, or is it a made-up service?
faqs.a: Instagram search matches text — name field, username, captions, alt text — so making that text match what buyers type is real, testable work. What's made up is the part sold as a growth hack: hashtag bundles, engagement pods, follow-unfollow. Search optimisation gets you found. It doesn't manufacture demand that isn't there.

faqs.q: How many hashtags should I use on Instagram in 2026?
faqs.a: Five to ten specific, relevant ones. Instagram has said adding more hashtags doesn't increase reach, and following hashtags was removed at the end of 2024. Treat them as categorisation, not distribution. Avoid engagement-bait tags — some are restricted, and a restricted tag can quietly limit the post.

faqs.q: Will my Instagram posts show up on Google?
faqs.a: Public content from professional accounts is eligible for Google indexing, and there's a setting in your privacy controls to opt out. Personal private accounts aren't. Whether a specific post ranks depends on the query and the competition, exactly as it would for any page. Write captions accordingly.

faqs.q: How much do Instagram SEO services cost in India?
faqs.a: Standalone "Instagram SEO" packages in India usually run ₹10,000–₹40,000 a month, and most of that is content production with the search work bundled in. We don't sell it standalone — it's a workstream inside our organic social retainer at ₹30,000, ₹50,000 or ₹70,000 a month, ex-GST.

faqs.q: Should I change my Instagram username to include keywords?
faqs.a: Usually no. Changing the handle breaks every existing link to your profile and Instagram doesn't redirect the old one. Put the keywords in the 30-character name field instead, which you can edit as often as you like with nothing breaking. Change the handle only if it's genuinely unrecognisable.

faqs.q: How long before Instagram SEO changes show anything?
faqs.a: Profile changes — name field, bio, highlights — can shift search-sourced discovery within two to four weeks because they apply to your whole back catalogue immediately. Caption and content changes compound more slowly, over eight to twelve weeks, since they only affect posts published after the change.
